basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum. Necdum terra germinabat, necdum vel ipsa, vel aquae'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et vidit Deus quod esset bonum. Necdum terra germinabat, necdum vel ipsa, vel aquae animantia viva produxerant, et tamen videre dicitur Deus quod esset bonum, cedentibus aquis, apparuisse aridam, quia videlicet aquae creator atque aestimator universitatis praevidens quae futura sunt, quasi perfecta jam laudat, quae adhuc in primi operis exordio sunt, nec mirum apud quem rerum perfectio non in consummatione operis, sed in suae est praedestinatione voluntatis.
